title: Don Jr.'s other government-contractor ties (Unusual Machines, 1789 portfolio)
summary: Unusual Machines is the strongest example. Don Jr. joined its advisory board on Nov 27, 2024 with 331,580 shares, and in Oct 2025 the company announced its largest Army order (3,500 drone motors, value undisclosed); in 2026 it was reported to be negotiating a Pentagon equity stake. Several 1789 portfolio companies won large federal awards after 1789's stakes became public: Anduril's Army enterprise agreement (ceiling up to $20B, Mar 2026), SpaceX and Anduril's Golden Dome interceptor awards (Apr 2026), plus Firehawk's small Air Force and Army awards. Those awards were competitive or multi-vendor, the companies' government business predates 1789, and no reporting ties any of them to 1789 or Don Jr. The Executive Branch club is a real Don Jr./1789 venture with no documented federal benefit. Every side denies intervention, and no reporting shows any.

sub_claims.statement: Don Jr. joined Unusual Machines as adviser and shareholder in Nov 2024.
sub_claims.finding: He was named to the advisory board on Nov 27, 2024, and the stock closed about 85% higher that day. The S-1 lists 331,580 shares: 131,580 from a private placement at $1.52 per unit and 200,000 under an RSU/advisory agreement. The FT put the stake at about $4M in Oct 2025.

sub_claims.statement: Unusual Machines won an Army contract after he joined.
sub_claims.finding: On Oct 15, 2025 the company announced its largest US government order: 3,500 motors and components for the 101st Airborne's A.B.E. V1.01 drones, with about 20,000 more parts planned for 2026. That was about 11 months after he joined. The value was not disclosed, and a $12.8M figure seen in one aggregator is unconfirmed.

sub_claims.statement: Don Jr. helped secure the Unusual Machines contract.
sub_claims.finding: No evidence was found. Both his spokesperson and the company deny he was involved, and CREW found no clear quid pro quo.

sub_claims.statement: Unusual Machines is in line for further federal benefits (Pentagon equity stake or loan).
sub_claims.finding: In May 2026 the Pentagon's National Economic Resilience Office was reported to be negotiating equity-stake funding with UMAC, PDW and Neros under the $1.1B Drone Dominance program. ProPublica reported that UMAC was under review for a Pentagon loan. No closed deal was found.

sub_claims.statement: His Unusual Machines advisory role is ongoing.
sub_claims.finding: CREW says the advisory agreement appears to have expired automatically after one year. His current shareholding is unclear. 2026 coverage (WSJ via Quartz, May 2026; IBTimes, 2026) still calls him a shareholder and advisory-board member, which conflicts with CREW's reading that the agreement expired. No company filing confirming either was found, so this remains unverified.

sub_claims.statement: 1789 Capital's portfolio includes Anduril, SpaceX, xAI, Cerebras and Firehawk.
sub_claims.finding: Firehawk is firmly documented: 1789 led its $60M Series C at about a $290M valuation, with the round dated either Jan or Sep 2025. The other four are listed as holdings by trade press and investor databases, some of them aggregators.

sub_claims.statement: Firehawk won federal awards after 1789's investment.
sub_claims.finding: Firehawk received a $4M Air Force TACFI contract, and in Aug 2026 it was named one of four Army Hydra-70 (AGR-21C) prototype awardees. Some of its AFRL/AFWERX/SBIR awards predate the round. The amounts are small, and nothing links them to Don Jr.

sub_claims.statement: Anduril, SpaceX/xAI and Cerebras won contracts or policy benefits timed to or because of Don Jr.'s involvement.
sub_claims.finding: Large federal awards did follow 1789's disclosed stakes, but none is tied by any source to 1789 or Don Jr. Anduril: the Army signed a 10-year enterprise agreement with a ceiling of up to $20B on 2026-03-13. It consolidates about 120 existing contracts, the ceiling is not an obligated amount, and the first task order was about $87M. 1789's Anduril stake was public by mid-May 2025. SpaceX and Anduril: both were among the 12 companies that won space-based-interceptor prototype awards for Golden Dome, worth up to $3.2B in total, in late April 2026. Accountable.US had flagged in May 2025 that 1789-linked firms were positioned for Golden Dome. xAI: the CDAO gave it a prototype deal with a $200M ceiling in July 2025, one of four identical awards (with OpenAI, Google and Anthropic), and later a GSA deal at 42 cents per agency. The date of 1789's xAI investment is not documented, so the sequence cannot be fixed. Cerebras: 1789 joined its $1.1B Series G on 2025-09-30. The CFIUS clearance for G42's stake was announced in March 2025, before 1789 invested. Cerebras listed on Nasdaq in May 2026. No federal contract tied to the investment was found. The big awards were competitive and went to several vendors, and these companies had large government businesses before 1789. Timing is documented; influence is not.

sub_claims.statement: The Executive Branch club is a Don Jr. venture tied to government benefits.
sub_claims.finding: The club itself is documented. It is an invite-only Georgetown club co-founded by Don Jr., Omeed Malik, Chris Buskirk and Alex and Zach Witkoff, with membership reported at about $500k. Its Apr 2025 launch drew at least six administration officials. No federal contract or benefit linked to it was found.

corrections: The Executive Branch club is a private members' club, not a government contractor. No federal contract or benefit tied to it was found.
The value of the Unusual Machines Army order was never disclosed. Dollar figures circulating online, such as $12.8M, are unconfirmed.

An earlier version of this file said only Firehawk had federal awards after 1789's investment. That was wrong. Anduril's Army enterprise agreement (ceiling up to $20B, March 2026) and the SpaceX and Anduril Golden Dome interceptor awards (April 2026) also came after 1789's stakes were public. Nothing ties those awards to 1789 or Don Jr., and they were multi-vendor or competitive.
denials_and_context: A Trump Jr. spokesperson told the FT, per summaries of its story, that he 'has never communicated with anyone in the administration on behalf of Unusual Machines or about the contract in question.' The company also denies he played any role.
1789 Capital says it is a passive minority growth-equity investor that does not call the government (see C26). Axios reports that Don Jr. is not on the growth fund's investment committee.
CREW and ethics experts find no clear quid pro quo and no legal bar on these roles. Their concern is the appearance of preferential access.
Context in their favor: NDAA-compliant drone motors and solid-rocket supply are genuine Pentagon shortfalls.
Research limits: citizensforethics.org and dronexl.co were blocked for direct fetch, and the shared web-search budget ran out before the Cerebras, Anduril and xAI checks.
